reader.requirement: An explicit or implicit CANCEL of a program also cancels every program directly or indirectly contained in it, as if a valid CANCEL were executed for each in reverse source order: each is reset to its initial state and its open internal files are implicitly closed.

edition-consulted.switches: folds DialectBehavior.CancelRefusesEveryActiveProgram (active from 2002) into BoundCancel: false at 85

refusesEveryActiveProgram selects the GR5 active test: at 85 the never-called active MAIN program is GR8's no-action case instead of EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE (kb/Work PB5241); every later step of CancelNode (GR8 test, GR4 cascade, implicit close, reset) is one arm for all editions

reader.edition-search: as for GR10: the cascade loop over Node.Children from last to first calls CancelNode with the CANCEL's own GR5 flag; CancelContained (INITIAL path) always passes true, which its comment justifies (no contained program is active there).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the cascade is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f02_10 covers one directly contained program with an open file; not exercised: an indirectly contained (depth 2) program, several siblings, a container cancelled through identifier-1, the reverse order

probes.printed: SL1 KA1 GG1 00 KB1 SL2 KA2 GG2 00 KB2 CANCELLED MAIN OPEN 00 MAIN GGGG SL1 KA1 GG1 00 KB1 (MATCH)
probes.expected: CANCEL identifier naming P4ASL resets P4ASL, its contained KA and KB and KA's contained GG (counters back to 1) and closes GG's open relative file (caller reads GGGG; GG's next OPEN OUTPUT 00)

probes.printed: CK1 KK1 ... CK2 KK2 ... AFTER 3 ... CK1 KK1 (MATCH)
probes.expected: cancel of P8ACK resets its contained P8AKK too

probes.printed: IY O 00 on both calls of INITIAL P3AIX (MATCH)
probes.expected: the implicit CANCEL of an INITIAL program cascades to its contained program (file closed, reopen 00)

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.5.3.4 GR4  (║5.3.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR4 -- 'all programs contained within the program referenced by the CANCEL statement are also cancelled'

reader.notes: The reverse source order is read from the loop over Node.Children; no probe made the order observable, since cancelling one contained program does not affect its siblings. The GR8 test runs before the cascade, which is sound because a contained program can only have been called after its container was.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-201/src/q4.cob (run q4-001, --std 85): separately compiled Q4P contains Q4A (which contains Q4AA) and COMMON sibling Q4B; Q4A calls Q4B and Q4AA. Printed 'P1 A1 B1 AA1 A1 B2 AA1 P2 A2 B3 AA2 A1 B4 AA1 M CANCELLED P P1 A1 B1 AA1 A1 B2 AA1 M SECOND CANCEL NO ACTION': CANCEL of Q4A resets Q4A and its contained Q4AA but not the COMMON sibling Q4B it called (B counts on), CANCEL of Q4P through a group identifier ('Q4P' + spaces) resets every program directly or indirectly contained in it (P1 A1 B1 AA1), and a second operand naming the just-cancelled Q4P is no action. CancelNode recurses over Node.Children last-to-first with no edition test; the reverse order is not observable (no probe made it so). The implicit CLOSE inside each cascaded CANCEL inherits the FILE STATUS defect recorded against 1985-GR-X.5.3.4-10 (same CloseFiles block); that is GR10's requirement, not GR4's. cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.3.4 GR4 'all programs contained within the program referenced by the CANCEL statement are also cancelled'.
